Actor Layer Capability Demo

SH-130, Texas · based on real recorded traffic data

Sample visualizations demonstrating actor-layer analysis capability, built as a proxy for the upcoming Georgia SR-307 intersection deployment (Georgia is not yet instrumented; Texas SH-130 production data stands in as a comparable). Several different real recorded events on this corridor were used, chosen for different reasons: one with a lighter, free-flowing character well suited to trajectory and kinematic-state demonstrations; one with heavier, sustained congestion better suited to queue-specific metrics; and others near ramps and lane changes chosen specifically for those capabilities.

Vehicle trajectories

SH-130 NB · based on a real recorded traffic event, July 13, 2026 · Clip: t=0s-90s, 22:29:54-22:31:24 UTC · 1x playback · 4 lanes + shoulder
Demonstrates actor-layer capability to track individual vehicle trajectories in real time, colored by speed, across a camera-verified 4-lane highway segment plus shoulder.
Assumption: speed-magnitude bins, not kinematic deceleration. Clip chosen as the densest 90s of activity rather than the full 47-minute incident.
0:00
stopped/crawling <7mph slow <22mph free flow

This card's scope

  • Clipped window: t=0s to 90s of the 47-min incident — real timestamps 22:29:54 to 22:31:24 UTC on 2026-07-13, chosen as the densest 90-second stretch (80 vehicles, wide speed spread 0.5-48 mph)
  • Same clip used on the deceleration/acceleration card, for consistency

Source columns (deployment.actors)

  • pos_x, pos_y, velocity_x, velocity_y, lane_id, observation_ts

Transformations

  • Speed = sqrt(velocity_x² + velocity_y²), m/s converted to mph for display
  • Position rotated by the corridor's true bearing (348°) into forward/lateral coordinates
  • 4 lane centers derived empirically from bearing-corrected lateral clustering, since cross-checked against the authoritative SH-130 HD-map lane data: all 4 lane_ids used in this clip (38220289-292) confirmed as lane_number 1-4, NB, within a single map segment

Thresholds

  • Stopped/crawling: speed < 3 m/s (~6.7 mph). Slow: speed < 10 m/s (~22 mph). These are speed-magnitude bins, not kinematic deceleration (that's the separate deceleration card)

Deceleration / acceleration states

SH-130 NB · same recorded event as the trajectories card above, July 13, 2026 · Clip: t=0s-90s, 22:29:54-22:31:24 UTC · 1x playback
Demonstrates actor-layer capability to classify vehicle kinematic state (stopped, decelerating, accelerating, steady) in real time, using the same clip as the trajectories card above, viewed a different way.
Assumption: kinematic state derived from velocity change over time, not the raw acceleration field (unpopulated). Clip chosen as the densest 90s for showing all four states together.
0:00
stopped/crawling decelerating accelerating out steady
States shown reflect what a vehicle did at least once during this window, not its state the whole time.

This card's scope

  • Clipped window: t=0s to 90s of the 47-min incident — real timestamps 22:29:54 to 22:31:24 UTC on 2026-07-13, chosen because it's the richest 90-second stretch for showing all four states together
  • 64 distinct vehicles present. At least once during this 90s window: 11 vehicles were stopped/crawling, 5 were decelerating, 12 were accelerating out. All 64 pass through a steady state at some point.
  • Median speed in this window is ~14.4 mph, genuinely slow, not free-flowing.
  • Same 4 lanes as the trajectories card above, cross-checked against the authoritative SH-130 HD-map lane data (confirmed lane_number 1-4, NB, single map segment).

Source columns (deployment.actors)

  • pos_x, pos_y, velocity_x, velocity_y, observation_ts

Transformations & thresholds

  • Acceleration derived from velocity change (raw acceleration_x/y field is 100% unpopulated), smoothed with a 3-sample rolling median, filtered to a physically plausible -12 to +6 m/s² range first
  • Stopped/crawling: speed < 3 m/s. Decelerating: smoothed accel < -2 m/s². Accelerating out: accel > +1.5 m/s² and speed < 20mph

Queue metrics

SH-130 NB · same recorded event as the trajectories card above, July 11, 2026 · 67 min window · road-aligned
This location experienced real, sustained queuing following a collision, letting these two distinct, separately-trackable queue capabilities be demonstrated on genuine queue behavior: when and how long a queue is present on the road, and how long individual vehicles sit in one. A third view, showing vehicles in spatial context colored by dwell time, is available as a separate card.
Queue presence & duration
Assumption: a qualifying cluster = 5+ vehicles under 3 m/s within 100ft. Demo threshold requires this sustained 10s+ (formal SH-130 definition requires 30s+, not reached in this sample — see About the data).

Source & method (this chart only)

  • pos_x, pos_y, velocity_x, velocity_y, observation_ts, sampled every 5s across the full 67-minute incident
  • At each sample, find the largest cluster of vehicles under 3 m/s within any 100ft span along the road, plot that count over time

Formal definition vs demo threshold

  • Formal: 5+ consecutive vehicles, same lane, 100ft span, adjustable speed threshold, sustained 30+ seconds
  • This SH-130 sample never sustains the full 30s continuously (max ~10-12s at any speed threshold tested: 3, 5, 7, 10 m/s). Demo threshold lowered to 10s+, stated here explicitly rather than silently redefined.
  • Congestion in this incident is diffuse, spread across most of the observed corridor rather than one tight cluster, which is why the formal 100ft/30s test doesn't fire.
Per-vehicle queued time
Assumption: queued = individual vehicle speed < 3 m/s (~6.7 mph), summed over the full incident, independent of nearby traffic.
Not shown above: one vehicle logged 839s queued, far beyond any other (next highest is 57s). It's excluded from the ranking because it reads as a vehicle stopped by the collision itself, not a routine queue participant — see "About the data" for the full check.

Source & method (this chart only)

  • Per actor, total seconds where instantaneous speed < 3 m/s (~6.7 mph), summed across the full incident, independent of nearby traffic or spatial clustering
  • One vehicle (839s total, reaching nearly 30 minutes of accumulated queued time) is excluded from this chart and shown as a footnote below instead, since it isn't representative of a queue participant, see note.

Footnote: the excluded vehicle

One tracked vehicle logged 839 seconds under 3 m/s across this incident, nearly 5x longer than the next highest (57s). Checked carefully: it enters normally, then has a 1840-second (~30.7 min) gap in tracking, reappears creeping under 3 m/s, and stays there continuously for 838s before departing. This reads as a vehicle involved in the collision or blocked immediately by it, not a routine queue participant, so it's excluded from the ranked comparison above rather than treated as "the top of the queue."

Queue in context

SH-130 NB · same recorded event as the trajectories/deceleration cards above, July 13, 2026 · Clip: t=0s-90s, 22:29:54-22:31:24 UTC · 1x playback · threshold <10mph · 4 lanes + shoulder
Same recorded event, window, lanes, and direction as the trajectories and deceleration cards, viewed a third way: individual vehicles colored by how long each has continuously been under a 10mph threshold, rather than by discrete speed bin or kinematic state.
Assumption: color reflects how long, continuously, each vehicle has been below 10mph at that moment, not a fixed stopped/moving category.

This card's scope

  • Uses the same recorded event as the trajectories and deceleration cards above, same window t=0s-90s, real timestamps 22:29:54-22:31:24 UTC on 2026-07-13, same 4 lanes + shoulder (camera-verified and cross-checked against the authoritative SH-130 HD-map lane data), same NB direction.
  • An earlier attempt used a different location to try to find a more dramatic queue example, but that location's lane data didn't hold up to verification (lateral std dev of 5-7m per lane, vs ~0.4-0.5m here), and a separate candidate location had a real direction-mixing contamination. Rather than keep chasing a "better" queue example on unverified ground, this uses the one location we've actually confirmed end to end.

Threshold

  • <10 mph, a middle ground between the trajectories card's 7mph "stopped/crawling" bucket and the 22mph "slow" bucket, chosen to give meaningful color variation without over-including most of this incident's actual traffic (median speed here is 14.4 mph)

Color encodes dwell time, not a fixed category

  • Blue = free-flowing or just started slowing, through amber, to red = continuously below 10mph. Max dwell observed in this clip is only ~9.6s, this incident's slowdowns are real but brief, not extended stops, consistent with what the deceleration card already shows

Lane changes & ramp exit trajectories

SH-130 SB · based on a real recorded traffic event, July 29, 2026 · 1x playback · 100s clip · mainline (3 lanes) + exit ramp
Demonstrates actor-layer capability to track vehicles changing lanes and vehicles leaving the highway via an exit ramp, verified against the authoritative SH-130 lane map. 10 vehicles complete a confirmed, sustained lane change (labeled "lane changing"). 4 vehicles complete a confirmed, continuous transition into the exit ramp (labeled "exiting"). All other traffic stays within a single mainline lane for the entire clip and is shown in blue for spatial context.
Assumption: lane geometry uses real lane_number positions from the authoritative SH-130 lane map. The ramp band is drawn as a diverging taper (illustrative of merge/exit direction, not a measured shape). Vehicles are colored and labeled by confirmed behavior: lane changing (green), exiting (amber), staying in lane (blue). Labels move with the vehicle for its full time on screen.
0:00
lane changing exiting via ramp staying in lane

About this card

  • 10 vehicles complete a confirmed, sustained lane change, settling into and staying in the new lane, not a momentary boundary crossing
  • 4 vehicles complete a confirmed, map-verified transition from the mainline into the exit ramp lane itself
  • Lane background uses real lane_number positions from the authoritative SH-130 HD-map lane data

Identifying a definitive lane change

  • Each vehicle's lateral position is classified against the 3 confirmed real lane centers (nearest-lane assignment), producing a lane-occupancy sequence over time.
  • That sequence is collapsed into contiguous dwell segments; segments shorter than 0.5s are treated as noise, not real lane occupancy.
  • A vehicle only counts as a confirmed lane change if it starts in one lane, ends in a different lane, and the net lateral shift between its first few and last few samples is at least 2.5m, roughly two-thirds of the 4m lane spacing. This excludes vehicles that merely drift near a lane boundary without completing a change.
  • Vehicles confirmed exiting are identified the same way, tracked continuously from a mainline lane into the ramp lane itself, not just approaching it.

Smoothing methodology

  • Only the lateral (cross-lane) coordinate is smoothed; forward position and speed are the original, unmodified pipeline output.
  • Each vehicle's lateral position at time t is replaced by a time-weighted Gaussian average of that vehicle's own lateral samples: weight = exp(-(t-t_j)^2 / (2·σ²)).
  • Vehicles confirmed staying in one lane use a wide smoothing window (σ = 1.05s), since a genuine straight-lane trajectory has almost no real curvature to preserve.
  • Vehicles confirmed lane-changing or ramp-exiting use a narrower window (σ = 0.3s), enough to remove sensor noise without blurring the real lateral movement of the maneuver itself.

Structural comparison: highway to intersection

Why SH-130 is a useful proxy, and where the analogy breaks down
Highway (SH-130, current)
Intersection (SR-307, Georgia)
Roadway geometry
  • Bidirectional, straight or gently curved corridor
  • No intersections, no traffic signals
  • Single flow direction per carriageway
  • Arterial with stop lights and turn lanes
  • Multiple approach legs converging at one node
  • Vehicle paths cross, merge, and diverge at the same point
Movement types
  • Free flow at speed
  • Deceleration into congestion
  • Stationary or stopped vehicles during backups
  • All movement is same direction, no turning
  • Left turn, right turn, and through movements, each with different queuing behavior
  • Signal-controlled stops rather than congestion-driven stops
  • Conflict points where crossing movements interact
What drives congestion / queuing
  • Recurring or non-recurring congestion from aggregate traffic flow (volume exceeding capacity)
  • Queue length is a function of flow state, not lane geometry
  • Queuing driven by signal timing and turn lane storage capacity
  • Left-turn queues are physically bounded by the turn pocket length, independent of overall flow
Observability constraints
  • Poles spaced roughly 200m apart, best tracking accuracy within about 100m of a camera
  • Virtual traffic counters drawn in these high-accuracy zones for counts and speeds
  • Pole placement already fixed, so observability is set by camera placement and road configuration
  • Varies by cluster: ~300ft of visibility on the Bourne Ave left turn (~12 cars), ~1/4 mile at the southwest cluster, ~650ft at the northeast T-junction cluster
  • Left-turn queue capacity is directly constrained by this shorter observability window
Aerial views: coverage zones
Three planned SR-307 deployment sites, shown against real aerial imagery with expected pole coverage overlaid. Each card marks where that coverage lines up with a specific use case: queue length and left-turn conflict points at the two unsignalized-driveway sites (B and C), and the merge/conflict point at the highway interchange (A). Distances shown are either calibrated measurements or the team's earlier observability estimates, labeled accordingly on each card.

Aerial coverage SITE A

SR-307 Location A · Jimmy Deloach Pkwy / Garden City Terminal West · 2 poles (A1, A2)
Coverage ↔ use case: pole coverage brackets the merge itself, where routing and collision-avoidance use cases would actually apply.

About this card

  • Location A provides continuous field-of-view coverage of the Jimmy Deloach Pkwy / SR-307 interchange and vehicles approaching from the Garden City Terminal West area, per the deployment plan
  • Corridor study finding: this segment has the highest crash frequency on SR-307, with disproportionate rear-end crashes; the SR-307/SR-21 intersection nearby shows queues up to 1,000ft at peak hours
  • Use cases: routing efficiency for distribution centers off Jimmy Deloach Pkwy (Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot), end-of-queue warning, red-light-violator/collision avoidance alerts
  • Repeated turn-lane arrow pavement markings are visible along the ramp approach, indicating a dedicated left-turn queue lane feeding the interchange

What's confirmed vs. approximate

  • Confirmed from the deployment plan: pole count, general coverage intent, and the corridor study finding figures
  • Confirmed, visible in this image: the turn-lane arrow markings along the ramp approach, and the gore where the ramp joins the mainline
  • Approximate: the ~650ft coverage figure is the team's earlier observability estimate, not a distance calibrated against this specific image (unlike Site C, this hasn't been cross-checked against a real geotiff measurement yet)
  • Approximate: the merge/conflict point and the left-turn queue lane path are placed by eye against the visible pavement markings, not a surveyed or lane-line-detected position

Coverage ↔ use case: pole coverage sits on the GFA entrance, both left-turn queue lanes, and both confirmed rail crossings, the use cases GDOT flagged here.

About this card

  • Corridor study finding: heavy congestion from the two at-grade rail crossings in this segment, high volume of rear-end collisions
  • Use cases: line-of-sight info to facilitate entry/exit into the unsignalized GFA facility, end-of-queue warning specifically at the rail crossings
  • Two distinct left-turn queue lanes are visible and annotated: one on the GFA approach (2 turn-arrow markings), one near Pole B1 on the Bourne Ave approach (3 turn-arrow markings)

What's confirmed vs. approximate

  • Confirmed, visible in this image: the GFA facility's curved entrance driveway, both at-grade rail crossings, and both left-turn queue lanes (5 total turn-arrow markings across the two lanes)
  • Approximate: the ~300ft Bourne Ave figure is the team's earlier observability estimate, not calibrated against this image
  • Not confirmed: the exact Bourne Ave curb cut itself; the queue lane near Pole B1 is the clearest visible proxy for that approach
